symbols.name: kernel scalar a
symbols.meaning: One of the two scalars of a two-point kernel $aI+bX$.
symbols.quote: Each frame change is a product of two-point kernels $aI+bX$, where $a$ and $b$ are the two scalars of the kernel, $I$ is the identity on two points, and $X$ is the swap of the two points.

symbols.name: kernel scalar b
symbols.meaning: The other scalar of a two-point kernel $aI+bX$.
symbols.quote: Each frame change is a product of two-point kernels $aI+bX$, where $a$ and $b$ are the two scalars of the kernel, $I$ is the identity on two points, and $X$ is the swap of the two points.

symbols.name: identity on two points
symbols.meaning: The identity map on the two points of a kernel.
symbols.quote: Each frame change is a product of two-point kernels $aI+bX$, where $a$ and $b$ are the two scalars of the kernel, $I$ is the identity on two points, and $X$ is the swap of the two points.

symbols.name: two-point swap
symbols.meaning: The map that swaps the two points of a kernel.
symbols.quote: Each frame change is a product of two-point kernels $aI+bX$, where $a$ and $b$ are the two scalars of the kernel, $I$ is the identity on two points, and $X$ is the swap of the two points.

relations.quote: A complex phase network is built on a [Subset-intersection network](subset-intersection-network.md), with a frame change on each edge.
Each frame change takes its scalars from [Gaussian dyadics](gaussian-dyadics.md), so sums and products stay exact with no rounding.
Its cost is controlled by the inclusions of [Subspace labels](subspace-labels.md) on its wires.
